summary: cluster_cap equals the single-trade risk rate (0.005) and is resolved on day-start equity while sizing uses current equity: after any same-day realised gain a near fully utilised candidate is rejected CLUSTER_CAP_REJECT on an empty book.
expected: A single candidate on an empty book, sized to the per-trade budget, is not rejected by the correlation cap.
actual: After a gain in the UTC day, a candidate with utilisation above day_start_equity/current_equity is rejected until 00:00 UTC; fine-step symbols (XRP, SOL, ETH, alt-coins) are hit, BTC passes because of its coarse step. The cluster comparison also runs for a candidate outside the cluster.
impact: No money lost (fails closed). Backtest and paper trade sets become dependent on booking order and step size: trades after a same-day win are removed, trades after a loss are kept. Live would refuse valid approvals with a misleading reason (as in incident 16-43).
evidence: portfolio.py:315-316 `cluster_sum = _add(cluster_open_risk, candidate_risk)`; `if cluster_sum > cluster_cap_quote`. ledger.py:104,156 thresholds resolved on day-start equity; ledger.py:193-198 apply_booking changes equity only; engine.py:858 sizes on ledger.equity; live_risk_inputs.py:15-19 'Two equities, on purpose'. Probe: day start 1000, +10 booked, XRP realised 5.0495 vs cap 5.000 -> CLUSTER_CAP_REJECT; day start 600, +6: XRP 3.0274, SOL 3.0075 vs 3.000 -> rejected.
why_tests_miss: Fixtures test the cap with open positions or equal equities; 16-43 fixed and tested the loss direction only.
recommendation: Owner choice: one equity base for the per-trade comparison, or a cluster cap above the single-trade risk; skip the cluster comparison for a candidate outside the cluster. Needs a new parameter set / strategy version and regenerated records.
known_prior: KNOWN:16-43 (loss direction only, closed 2026-11-08); gain direction not recorded

component: adverse-edge sizing, R denominator, utilisation gate
rule: D046 item 2 (Phase 12 D-03); RISK_MANAGEMENT lines 34-41; Phase 14 D-20
summary: Positions are sized as if the entry filled at the adverse zone edge, but the entry is a single LIMIT at the zone mid, so that fill cannot occur: a stopped-out Family A trade loses about 60 % of the stated risk budget and R multiples use the larger figure.
expected: The configured risk (0.5 % of equity) is about what a stopped-out trade loses; an R multiple of -1 means a full stop.
actual: Family A real loss at the stop is 59-61 % of budget (about 0.30 % of equity), Family B 93 %, Family C 89 %. realized_risk (the R denominator) is the adverse-edge figure, so a full stop-out books about -0.6 R for Family A.
impact: Safe side for money. R figures of the three families are on different scales; the 1 % daily stop equals about 3.3 Family A stop-outs instead of 2; the 60 % utilisation floor is really about 36 % for Family A; the owner reads 0.5 % for a trade that can lose 0.3 %.
evidence: gating.py:14-19 'Sizing uses the ADVERSE edge ... The zone mid REMAINS ... the price the order is actually placed at'; planner.py:150-156, 609-610 (zone pivot +/-0.5 ATR, range +/-0.6 ATR, stop pivot-0.8 ATR); placement.py:118-133 derive_limit_price = zone mid. Probe: equity 1000, budget 5.00: Family A recorded realized_risk 4.9964, loss at stop for a fill at the limit incl. costs 3.0482. D046: 'decided in the unattended run without a checkpoint'.
why_tests_miss: Property tests assert loss <= budget, which holds; nothing asserts the reachable loss is close to the budget.
recommendation: Owner choice: keep and document the real per-family risk, or size at the placed limit price (changes quantities, needs regenerated records).
known_prior: KNOWN:D046 item 2 (consequence stated in words, not quantified for the Phase 15 geometry)

rule: AGENTS 'Fail closed: uncertain data => NO_TRADE'; no future-candle leakage
summary: The pure core never checks that the 4h context stream ends at (or just before) the evaluated 1h bar: a context 90 days stale, or 8 hours in the future, still yields a regime verdict.
expected: A context stream older than one context interval, or newer than the evaluated bar, gives DATA_STALE in the core.
actual: The regime is computed from whatever the caller passes; the callers' bisect cut prevents future bars but not a missing newest 4h bar.
impact: A late or missing newest 4h bar makes the direction filter use a stale regime and paper/live differ from the backtest for the same bar, with no reason code. Reachability from the runtimes not traced (other lanes).
evidence: strategy.py:693-735 per-stream checks only; types.py:285-291 MarketSnapshot checks types only. Probe: context aligned / -10 days / -90 days / +8 hours all return regime=BULLISH, none DATA_STALE.
why_tests_miss: Tests feed aligned fixtures; the gap test injects a gap inside a stream, never a trailing one.
recommendation: In evaluate, return DATA_STALE unless setup_close - context_interval < context_last_close <= setup_close.

rule: D-02 / STRAT-01 (never source a SETUP from an unclosed candle)
summary: The core forming-bar gate compares close_time with prev close + duration; a forming Binance kline carries its scheduled close time, so the gate cannot detect it. The test uses a bar shape the exchange does not send.
expected: The core recognises an unclosed bar, or the docs state the rule is enforced upstream only.
actual: _is_forming_bar returns False for a Binance-style forming bar. The effective guards are upstream (paper loop double gate x=True AND close<=now; REST filters).
impact: False assurance: a future caller that trusts the core gate would evaluate a forming bar. No bypass of the upstream guards was found in the paper path; live path belongs to another lane.
evidence: strategy.py:90-92 `expected_close = prev.close_time_utc + duration; return candle.close_time_utc < expected_close`. tests/test_candle_close_timing.py:170-180 builds the forming bar with close = open + 1h30m. Probe: _is_forming_bar(forming, prev) = False.
why_tests_miss: Test and code were written from the same misunderstanding of the kline format.
recommendation: Document the gate as a chaining check and keep the clock-based rule at every entry point, or pass an explicit as-of close into evaluate.

rule: Phase 15 D-16/D-27 (PLACEHOLDER sets are refused for paper); 16-DEC-O-02 item 2
summary: The 48 research-run sets carry the same unvalidated seed values as baseline-v6 but label them EXPERIMENT instead of PLACEHOLDER, so the gate that refuses PLACEHOLDER values for paper sees zero.
expected: A gate that keeps values without a basis out of paper/live cannot be passed by renaming the label.
actual: PLACEHOLDER-key count: baseline-v6 16/17/22, research-run-1-a01/b01/c01 0, with identical values and 'no empirical basis yet' text. The gate reads only the label.
impact: None for money now (SHADOW paper). For mainnet the provenance labels cannot serve as go-live evidence; a go-live gate keyed on PLACEHOLDER would also see zero.
evidence: rationale.py:199 `table.get("basis") == "PLACEHOLDER"`; research-run-1-a01.toml:107-110 basis EXPERIMENT, value 2.0, text '... no empirical basis yet. Held fixed by the research-run-1 preregistration ... not evidence that the value is good.'; 16-DEC-O-02 item 2 'EXPERIMENT means fixed and preregistered before any result, not shown to be good; no PLACEHOLDER label'.
why_tests_miss: Tests check that a label exists and is well formed, not what it means.
recommendation: Owner choice: a separate label (e.g. PREREGISTERED) that paper may accept and live must refuse, or a go-live rule refusing EXPERIMENT without a result reference.

rule: registry docstring 'loader is fail-closed'; AGENTS 'Fail closed'
summary: The registry has no required-key list and no range check for the portfolio, daily-loss, utilisation and RR keys: a set with cluster_cap = -1, utilisation floor 0, daily stop 100 % or without min_stop_atr loads.
expected: Out-of-range risk limits or a family set without its required keys refuse to load.
actual: They load; some silently disable a gate (min_stop_atr absent, utilisation 0), some raise KeyError at the first bar (touch_tolerance_atr absent).
impact: Low: every set is hash-pinned and needs a new committed file. Matters because sets are written by agents in bulk and the owner cannot review numbers by eye.
evidence: registry.py:347-399 ranges only rate keys, cost guards, TTL, pivot widths, geometry_version, min_stop_atr. Probe on range-mr baseline-v6 text: LOADS with cluster_cap=-1, max_aggregate_open_risk=5, minimum_risk_utilization_after_rounding=0, daily_loss_stop_threshold=1, minimum_rr=-3, max_open_positions=1000, min_stop_atr removed, touch_tolerance_atr removed.
why_tests_miss: Tests cover the keys that have ranges.
recommendation: Per-family required keys; ranges for the five portfolio/daily keys, the utilisation floor, minimum_rr and max_open_positions.

rule: AGENTS 'Invariants that are machine-enforced' (Decimal-only, no wall clock, src/core pure)
summary: The float guard lists core/domain/risk files by hand and omits cost_rates.py, cost_guards.py, _decimal.py, lot_filters.py, transitions.py, live_commission.py; no wall-clock guard is applied to src/core or the Phase 5 risk modules; the import-purity test omits pivots.py and _decimal.py.
expected: The guards cover every module of the packages they are said to protect, including files added later.
actual: All these files are clean today (0 float shapes, 0 wall-clock calls), but a float or datetime.now() added to one of them would not fail CI.
impact: Latent; the money cost producer (cost_rates.py) is among the unguarded files.
evidence: tests/test_domain_no_float.py:16-101 explicit list, line 139 globs only for src/backtest, src/paper, src/research. tests/test_core_tracer.py:395 names five core files. Own scan output probe_guards.out marks the six files NOT_FLOAT_SCANNED.
why_tests_miss: Hand-kept list; the registration trap was fixed for three packages only.
recommendation: Glob src/core/*.py, src/domain/*.py, src/risk/*.py in the float guard and add one wall-clock + import test over the same globs.

rule: AGENTS Quantization; owner goal small capital
summary: With 500 USDT and 0.5 % risk, BTCUSDT is tradable only for stops between about 0.8 % and 2.35 % (27 of 115 grid points); at 1000 USDT 72 of 115 with utilisation-reject bands. Other symbols are limited only by the cost ceiling.
actual: The BTC trade set depends on account equity and on where the stop falls relative to the 0.001 step.
impact: Research figures for BTC are equity-dependent; live will show many MIN_QTY / UTILIZATION rejections on BTC. Mainnet BTCUSDT minimum notional not verified (fixture says 50).
evidence: probe_sizing.out section B: BTCUSDT eq 500: tradable 27/115, widest SL 2.35 %, rejects COST_TO_RISK_EXCEEDED 10, UTILIZATION_REJECT 5, MIN_QTY_REJECT 73; eq 1000: 72/115, widest 4.85 %.
recommendation: Owner choice: accept, drop BTC from the small-account universe, or revisit the 60 % utilisation floor.
known_prior: partly KNOWN:D046 item 6 (cost ceiling binds at about 0.79 %)

summary: invalidation_rule_json carries break_distance_atr, whose value is a price distance (sl_buffer_atr x ATR), not ATR multiples, and which no code reads; it is part of the plan hash.
expected: A hashed field is read by something and its name matches its unit.
impact: None today; a future reader trusting the name would be wrong by a factor of ATR; renaming changes plan hashes.
evidence: planner.py:691-697 `break_distance = _mul(sl_buffer_atr, atr)` ... `"break_distance_atr": str(break_distance)`; grep finds only writers (backtest/case.py:507, paper/rehearsal.py:428).
